extracted.intended_audience: press release writers, public relations professionals, and journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for structuring press releases using the inverted-pyramid journalism model: front-load essential facts, order supporting detail by importance, and place quotes/background at the end so releases are journalist-friendly and easily edited or indexed.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Lead (Top): most newsworthy details
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lead (Top): The most newsworthy details, answering who, what, where, when, why, and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inverted pyramid's widest part at the top represents the most substantial, interesting, and important information. Put the lead first so readers and editors immediately see the core news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-load most important information in the first 30 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Front-loads the most important information in the first 30 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly advises that the most important information should appear very early (first 30 words) to ensure immediate comprehension and to fit how reporters scan copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all 5Ws + H in the first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers all 5Ws + H in the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 5Ws (who, what, where, when, why) and how should fit in the first paragraph; this makes the story self-contained at the top and easier for journalists to reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order subsequent paragraphs in descending importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders subsequent paragraphs in descending importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the lead, organize supporting facts and context so each paragraph is less essential than the one above it; this creates a clear information hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details (Middle): supporting facts, background, context
rubrics_metrics.description: The Details (Middle): Supporting facts, background, and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the middle section to provide additional facts and context that explain or substantiate the lead; these are important but expendable if space is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extras (Bottom): quotes, company background, additional info
rubrics_metrics.description: The Extras (Bottom): Quotes, company background, and additional info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place quotes and organizational background toward the end of the release where they add color and depth but are the easiest material to cut for length or editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can be cut from the bottom without losing essential meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Can be cut from the bottom without losing essential meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inverted pyramid allows editors to 'cut from the bottom' so that removing lower paragraphs preserves the essential facts and readability of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes and background details come last
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes and background details come last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit guidance to place quotations and company background in the Extras section so that the core news remains at the top and editing/removal of extras does not harm the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make releases journalist-friendly to increase pickup likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure is journalist-friendly, aligning with how reporters are trained to write. Press releases that follow the inverted pyramid are more likely to be picked up because they require less editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing releases to match reporters' expectations (lead-first, clear 5Ws, descending importance) improves chances of media pickup and reduces reporter workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place keywords and critical facts early for SEO and AI indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Search engines and AI tools prioritize content with clear information hierarchies. Placing keywords and critical facts early helps releases get indexed and surfaced in search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond human readers, front-loading important facts and keywords aids discoverability in search engines and AI summarizers; include key terms near the top of the release.
